Sts. Adam and Eve

Introduction

The Orthodox calendar names the first-created Sts. Adam and Eve among the righteous remembered before Christ’s Nativity.

Read circumstances and sources

The first-created in Genesis

Genesis presents Sts. Adam and Eve as the first human pair. Humanity is created in God’s image, and the account describes life in Eden, the command concerning the tree and the relationship of man and woman. These passages establish the biblical setting of their names and their place in Christian teaching about humanity.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Genesis 1:26–28; 2:7–25

The fall and its consequences

The serpent’s temptation, the eating of the forbidden fruit and the attempt to hide from God are narrated in Genesis 3. The consequences include suffering, exclusion from Eden and mortality. The story also records God’s provision of clothing. This profile follows the text without supplying imagined conversations beyond it.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Genesis 3:1–24

Death and limits of the account

Genesis reports Adam’s death at 930 years of age. It does not give an equivalent account of Eve’s death. These are the scriptural narratives; neither a modern absolute chronology nor a separate martyrdom story is established here.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Genesis 5:1–5

Christian remembrance

The OCA explicitly includes Sts. Adam and Eve in the Sunday before the Nativity. Their commemoration belongs to that movable Sunday, rather than a fixed date taken from one year’s calendar.

[1] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Opening sentence identifying Sts. Adam and Eve

Romans contrasts the consequences of Adam’s disobedience with Christ’s saving obedience. First Corinthians similarly contrasts Adam and Christ in its teaching about death and resurrection.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Romans 5:12–21; 1 Corinthians 15:21–22,45–49
